items.title: 66600_Teddy Wilson oral history interview
items.q: Like John, over here, Ben -- and his name is Fabricious.

ctx.x: But I had just left Chicago, working with Louis Armstrong, you know, and to me Billie was like a girl doing a take-off on Armstrong. It was novel, no one else had thought to do it, no other girl singing whose sound (inaudible). Ella certainly wasn't. Ella was doing her own thing, strictly. So I found Ella much more attractive in her singing, than Billie.

John liked Billie and the public, and you can't write that off. Billie was a big success. One thing about Billie, she could sing -- she had a very strong gift in that she could sing five seconds and her name was written all over the music. You knew it was Billie Holiday and no one else. That is a great asset to anyone.
